claims.statement: On CoffeeBean and CoffeeBeanDiffUpdate, tasting_notes is a list[str] described as flavour notes in the order they appear in the description; the raw notes come from roaster descriptions and are categorized post-hoc by AI rather than being structured objects on the bean record.

The clean_tasting_notes field validator enforces three normalization invariants on the tasting_notes array: every note is title-cased via .strip().title(), duplicates are removed while preserving first-seen order with a seen set, and long descriptive single-note strings are split via split_tasting_notes_if_needed before the dedup/title pass.

split_tasting_notes_if_needed only attempts AI splitting when the array has exactly one element whose note is longer than 15 characters and contains a sentence-like marker (' with ', ' and ', ' notes of ', '. ', ', '); it constructs a TastingNoteSplitter and runs it in a dedicated ThreadPoolExecutor thread only when GOOGLE_API_KEY is set, and silently falls back to the original notes on any failure.

TastingNoteSplitter is a PydanticAI agent backed by gemini-3.1-flash-lite with thinking disabled (thinking_budget 0) whose system prompt extracts individual concise Title-Cased flavour notes from long descriptive strings, strips filler/marketing language, preserves already-separated notes, keeps acidity/sweetness context, and returns a single-item list when the input is one flavour description rather than a list; it returns TastingNotesSplit with a notes list and falls back to [text.strip().title()] on error or short input.

The tasting-note taxonomy is a strict three-tier hierarchy of primary → secondary → tertiary category; TastingNoteCategory enforces via a model_validator that a tertiary_category is only allowed when a secondary_category is also present (raising otherwise), and the categorization agent's system prompt reinforces that a tertiary requires a secondary and a secondary requires a primary.

taste_lexicon.json is a controlled vocabulary with a _meta block (comment, last_updated, warning that AI-generated tertiary additions should be reviewed) and a categories array; each category block carries primary_category, optional secondary_category, tertiary_category (null), and a flavors array of valid tertiary terms for that branch, and the categorizer injects the entire JSON into the LLM system prompt.

TastingNoteCategorizer orchestrates three PydanticAI agents all backed by gemini-3.5-flash: a categorization agent (output TastingNoteBatch) assigning primary/secondary/tertiary plus confidence, a naming agent (output CanonicalNameBatch) extracting canonical flavour words more specific than the parent secondary for lexicon expansion, and a non-flavour check agent (output NonFlavourCheckBatch) detecting product names, locations, marketing phrases, and codes.
categorize_batch sends notes to the categorization agent and on exception falls back to assigning every note primary_category 'Other' with confidence 0.1, so batch failures never abort the run.

update_lexicon_with_new_tertiary_categories groups CSV rows that have a secondary but no tertiary, runs the naming agent to extract canonical names, and adds any name appearing at least min_count (default 3) times that is not already in the lexicon to the matching category's flavors list, then re-sorts the list and re-saves taste_lexicon.json with an updated _meta timestamp and warning.

recategorize_other_notes re-processes notes bucketed as 'Other': the non-flavour agent classifies each, genuine flavours are re-run through the categorization agent to find a proper category, and non-flavours (product names, locations, marketing phrases, altitude values, codes) are marked with primary_category 'None' and confidence 0.0; the agent leans towards is_flavour=True when in doubt and defaults to is_flavour=True on failure.

The categorizer is run via a Typer CLI whose categorize command supports --update-missing (re-categorize existing notes lacking a tertiary), --cleanup (interactively remove CSV notes no longer in the database), and --recategorize-other (run the Other-bucket non-flavour cleanup); default mode processes only notes present in the DB but not yet in the CSV, and every run finishes by calling update_lexicon_with_new_tertiary_categories.

tasting_notes_categorized.csv is the materialized categorizer output with columns tasting_note, primary_category, secondary_category, tertiary_category, confidence; it is a flat lookup from a raw note string to its hierarchy position and includes foreign-language terms, compound descriptions, and non-flavour entries flagged with None categories and confidence 0.0.

At API startup load_tasting_notes_categories clears the tasting_notes_categories DuckDB table and bulk-loads tasting_notes_categorized.csv via read_csv_auto, then creates the coffee_beans_with_categorized_notes view that joins each bean to its notes' categories through unnest(tasting_notes) and aggregates primary_categories, secondary_categories, tertiary_categories, and avg_categorization_confidence per bean.

GET /v1/tasting-note-categories accepts the full standard bean filter set, unnests each filtered bean's tasting_notes, joins to tasting_notes_categories, excludes rows whose lowercased primary_category is in ('none','null','no match'), groups by the full primary→secondary→tertiary hierarchy, and returns per-group note_count, total_bean_count, tasting_notes, and tasting_notes_with_counts structs plus a categories dict keyed by primary category and metadata; it is cached with SimpleMemoryCache.

GET /v1/search/by-tasting-category takes a required primary_category, optional secondary_category, and min_confidence (default 0.5), joins coffee_beans to tasting_notes_categories filtering by those categories and confidence, and returns paginated APISearchResult objects ordered by average categorization confidence with pagination metadata.

On read paths such as /v1/search the API decorates each tasting note with its primary_category via a correlated subselect packing struct_pack(note, primary_category) over unnest(tasting_notes); APICoffeeBean.tasting_notes is typed list[TastingNote | str] to accept either the decorated {note, primary_category} structs or plain strings, and the original note order is preserved through this decoration.

The /flavours route loader calls /v1/tasting-note-categories forwarding all URL filter parameters and returns grouped categories plus metadata; the page renders a D3 SunburstChart whose inner ring is the primary category, middle ring the secondary, and outer ring the tertiary with individual tasting notes as leaves, with click-to-zoom, mobile pinch-to-zoom/pan, double-tap reset, and onTastingNoteClick adding a note to the search filters.

transformToSunburstData builds the hierarchical tree for the SunburstChart from the flat API response; it flattens any 'General' placeholder node directly into its parent, caps leaf notes per tertiary node at TASTING_NOTE_THRESHOLD (10), and buckets remaining notes under an isOther-flagged 'Other' node (or attaches a lone remainder directly), letting D3 sum parent values from the leaves.

The frontend defines a canonical FLAVOUR_CATEGORY_ORDER array (Fruity, Floral, Sweet, Nutty, Cocoa, Spicy, Roasted, Earthy, Green/Vegetative, Sour/Fermented, Sour/Acid, Alcohol/Fermented, Chemical, Papery/Musty, Cereal, Mouthfeel, Amplitude, Spices, Taste Basics, Other) for consistent display ordering and getFlavourCategoryHexColor assigning each primary category a stable hex colour, used by both the SunburstChart and FlavourProfileDonut.

GET /v1/flavour-images scans the data/flavours/paintings directory for .jpg files, derives the note name from each filename (unicode-normalized, underscores to spaces), and enriches each with attribution (author, licence, licence URL) looked up from wikidata_flavour_images.json; the flavours/+layout.ts loader fetches this list once and the flavourImageService looks up a matching image for the hovered note.

FlavourProfileDonut renders a layerchart donut on the roaster detail page from a categories array of {primary_category, count, percentage}; it sorts slices by FLAVOUR_CATEGORY_ORDER, hides callout labels for slices below 2% while force-showing the hovered slice's label and dimming the rest, and displays the total note count in the centre.

The roaster detail endpoint computes flavour_categories by joining the roaster's beans' tasting notes to tasting_notes_categories, excluding Taste Basics, Mouthfeel, and Amplitude so the profile reflects actual flavour descriptors, and only builds the profile when there are at least 3 categorised flavour notes; each category's percentage is its share of that roaster's categorised notes.

The guided tasting wizard (TastingWizard.svelte and lib/tasting/conversation.ts) uses the SCA flavour lexicon as its category backbone with category-specific guided questions, defect mappings, and sensory intensity scales; mergeDynamicFlavours merges live note-frequency data from /v1/tasting-note-categories into the hardcoded skeleton so the flavour chips reflect actual database prevalence, and the wizard state machine runs basics→overview→category→mouthfeel→summary with sessions persisted client-side in IndexedDB via Dexie.
